cloze.title: 原文选词填空
cloze.instruction: 从词库中选择合适的词填入空白，每词使用一次，保留原文词形。大小写不影响判分。

parts.text: These terms are often used interchangeably, although they mean different things. “Natural” usually describes ingredients

from natural sources. “Herbal” refers to plant-based ingredients, while “organic” generally describes ingredients produced to particular farming standards. None of these labels, on its own, shows that a toothpaste can prevent tooth

.

The range of products is considerable. A 2021 UK study examined 500 toothpastes, from 95 brands with alternative formats such as tooth powders and solid toothpaste tablets. Nearly a third contained no fluoride, and some did not clearly state their fluoride

. The study examined products available to buy, so it cannot tell us how many people actually use fluoride-free toothpaste.

Why fluoride makes a difference

Tooth decay begins when bacteria in dental plaque, a

film that builds up on teeth, feed on sugars from food and drinks. They produce acids that damage enamel, the hard outer surface of the tooth. Over time, this can lead to holes, or cavities.

Fluoride helps enamel resist acid and

early damage before a cavity forms. Its benefits are supported by decades of research. A 2019 Cochrane review, which brought together results from 96 studies, found that brushing with fluoride toothpaste reduced tooth decay compared with brushing with toothpaste without fluoride. Reviews bring together findings from

studies to assess the overall evidence.

Yet people sometimes switch to fluoride-free products because they believe natural ingredients must be safer or healthier.

In a 2019 letter to the British Dental Journal, my
and I described a dental student who had developed several cavities after changing to a fluoride-free organic toothpaste. The student had other risk factors, including a history of

snacking and infrequent dental visits. We can not say that this single case cannot show that the organic toothpaste caused multiple decays, but this clearly illustrates why checking for fluoride is important, even for people who brush their teeth

.

The evidence for herbal toothpaste

Some toothpastes and mouthwashes contain plant extracts, including green tea, aloe vera and neem, a tree traditionally used for oral hygiene in South Asia. These ingredients may help control bacteria and gum
– also called gingivitis – which can cause redness, swelling and bleeding when brushing.

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

The physical properties of foods explain why freezing and thawing affect their textures differently.
